passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of three different cognitive training programs on working memory performance in adults aged 20-30. The study was a randomized controlled trial with four groups: a control group that received no training, and three treatment groups that received Training A (visual-spatial), Training B (verbal), and Training C (mixed). Each group had 30 participants. After a 4-week intervention, participants completed a standardized working memory task. Table 1 shows the mean reaction times (in milliseconds) and standard deviations for each group. The researchers hypothesized that Training C would yield the greatest improvement, followed by Training A and Training B, with the control group showing the least improvement. The results indicated a reduction in reaction time for all training groups compared to control, with the largest effect observed in Training C. The authors concluded that mixed-modality training may be most effective for enhancing working memory in young adults.
table_data:
Group | Sample Size | Mean RT (ms) | SD (ms)
Control | 30 | 650 | 45
Training A | 30 | 580 | 50
Training B | 30 | 600 | 48
Training C | 30 | 520 | 55
stem: Which group had the lowest mean reaction time after the intervention?
explanation: The table shows that Training C had the lowest mean reaction time of 520 ms, indicating the greatest improvement.
trap: Choosing the control (650 ms) by treating the highest reaction time as best; a lower reaction time means faster responses.

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the study’s findings?

options.A: Mixed‑modality training gave a lower mean RT than either single‑modality training in adults aged 20–30, but the data do not show whether older adults benefit.
options.B: Verbal training was no better than no training.
options.C: Training had no effect on reaction time.
options.D: Older adults benefit more than young adults.

explanation: Correct: Training C (520 ms) was below Training A (580 ms) and Training B (600 ms) in adults aged 20–30; no older adults were studied. Why the others are wrong: B) Training B (600 ms) was lower than control (650 ms). C) All three training groups were below control. D) Only adults aged 20–30 were studied.
trap: Generalizing to other age groups or to prior literature; only adults aged 20–30 were tested.
